OK, everyone, it is nine o'clock, and we have to present the case at eight tomorrow morning. Let's divide up the work. Kenji, you know the numbers, so you have to check the figures. Ana, can you write a draft of the slides? I will present the problem, and someone else has to present the recommendation. We don't have to finish everything tonight, but we must agree on the recommendation before we leave this room. Tomorrow we meet at seven to rehearse. Twenty minutes, not more. And please, everybody contributes. Nobody has to be perfect.

In my study group, I was the quiet one for two days. I thought, I don't have to speak, the others are better at this. On Wednesday, a woman from Singapore looked at me and said, you have to tell us what you think, you are the only banker here. So I volunteered to present the numbers the next morning. I rehearsed three times in my hotel room. The presentation was not perfect, but after that, the group asked for my opinion on every case. My advice is simple. You don't have to speak a lot. But you must speak early.
